purpose: How a plating-bench operator physically executes a gold run: choosing rack, barrel or brush per piece geometry and batch size, placing contacts where marks will not show while current still flows honestly, spacing and orienting parts so every surface sees solution, managing drag-out and the inter-tank rinse sequence so no chemistry poisons the next tank, running the transfer clock on perishable surfaces, closing the run with rinse-dry-first-touch discipline, and logging every job to its parameters so results can be reproduced, diagnosed and defended.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the piece arrives plate-ready and the baths arrive healthy: substrate triage, mechanical finishing, chemical prep and bath maintenance are owned by upstream specialists and trusted as done

the thickness target with its measurement points comes from the electrical-control KB and the layer stack with its compliance flags comes from the layer-architecture KB; this KB executes the physical run those specs describe

all plating chemistry is a purchased commercial product operated per its supplier technical data sheet (TDS); every numeric window mentioned here is a mechanism, a handbook-class reference, or a corpus-tagged class, never an asserted setpoint
rectifiers, barrels, agitation hardware and stripping lines are operated within their equipment manufacturer's instructions; anything beyond that boundary goes to a qualified technician
workplace, hazmat, waste and marking rules vary by jurisdiction and must be verified locally; safety statements here are obligation classes plus formal-training pointers, not procedures
exclusions: electrical control and thickness delivery: surface-area estimation methods, current density as the master variable, Faraday-based time-thickness estimation, cathode efficiency, rectifier setup and verification, current-distribution mapping, shielding, robbers-as-current-tools and auxiliary-anode classes belong to the electrical-control KB; this KB reports the loaded area facts (piece count, exposed rack metal, robbers present) that the amps calculation consumes and executes the load plan that calculation requires

layer architecture: strike-layer selection, barrier underplates (nickel as a class with its nickel-release compliance flag, palladium and white bronze as nickel-free classes, copper leveling), diffusion mechanisms, flash-vs-heavy build per wear class, duplex systems and post-plate topcoats belong to the layer-architecture KB; when a stack containing nickel serves skin-contact goods, this KB carries the nickel-release compliance flag through the run plan and log untouched, with verify-your-jurisdiction attached, and never adjudicates it

bath chemistry: gold system selection, analysis, replenishment and contamination diagnosis belong to the bath-chemistry specialist; this KB manages what the work physically carries between tanks, not what is in them

prep-chain execution: degrease, electroclean, water-break testing, pickle and activation chemistry belong to the surface-prep specialist; this KB owns the clock and handling between those steps and the gold, not the chemistry of them

numeric setpoints asserted as fact: rotation speeds, dwell seconds, rinse conductivities, temperatures and timings are mechanisms and equipment-instruction or TDS classes; the specific product documents and the shop's own logged runs govern actual numbers

mains-side electrical work, rectifier internals, improvised splices or undersized leads: rigging stays within the rack, barrel and rectifier manufacturer's instructions, and anything beyond goes to a qualified electrician
forcing a piece that cannot be racked, clipped or contacted without damage: that piece is escalated to intake and the customer decision path with options documented, never improvised onto the line

quality verification and claim approval: XRF measurement, adhesion testing, color adjudication and marking-term compliance belong to the quality and marking specialists; this KB hands them a logged, contact-mapped lot
personalized legal, medical or financial advice, including nickel-allergy guidance, which routes to regulation classes and professional care

competency_questions.question: How do I turn this job sheet into a physical run plan before anyone touches a piece?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RUN_PLAN_FROM_JOB_SPEC produces a written plan naming route, tank order, fixture, contact zones, masking and the compliance flags carried through from the stack spec, with unfixturable pieces flagged for escalation at planning time

competency_questions.question: Rack, barrel or brush for this piece and this batch size - how is the call made and defended?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROCESS_ROUTE_DECISION gives the fitness test per route with RACK_ROUTE_CLASS and BARREL_ROUTE_CLASS supplying the mechanism behind each route's virtues and hard exclusions, and the decision is recorded with its reason

competency_questions.question: Where do I contact this piece so the mark will not show, and what do I do when the hidden spot cannot carry the current?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTACT_POINT_PLACEMENT names the hidden-feature preference, the contact-sized-to-current rule, and the ordered fallbacks (mid-run contact move, planned brush touch-up zone, escalation) when hiding and current capacity collide

competency_questions.question: What must be true of the rack itself before I trust it with a load, and how do fixtures age out?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RACK_WIRING_INTEGRITY requires per-run continuity, coating and tip checks with exposed rack metal reported to the area estimate, and FIXTURE_MAINTENANCE_LIFECYCLE sets the stripping, repair and retirement cadence driven by the fixture-linked defect record

competency_questions.question: How do I space and orient parts so every piece sees solution and current, none shadows its neighbor, and no hollow traps gas or solution?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOAD_SPACING_AND_ORIENTATION covers spacing, anode facing, field-edge positions and the closed area estimate, and PART_VENTING_DRAINAGE covers the tilt discipline that vents bubbles and drains cups before agitation is asked to fix what geometry sealed

competency_questions.question: Which agitation class does this run need, and which agitation choices are unsafe or useless where?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AGITATION_DELIVERY names the bench agitation classes including barrel rotation and nib motion, states the mist-control flag on air-agitated nickel-bearing tanks, and bounds what agitation can and cannot reach

competency_questions.question: How do I stop each tank's chemistry from riding into the next one, and where does the gold in dragged-out solution go?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DRAG_OUT_CONTROL gives the withdrawal, dwell and drainage levers with gold-bearing streams routed to labeled recovery, and RINSE_SEQUENCE_DESIGN designs the counterflow cascade, dead rinse before gold, conductivity gates and rinse identity that keep chemistries apart

competency_questions.question: How fast must a piece move between tanks, and what happens when the line stalls with an activated surface in the air?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRANSFER_TIMING_DISCIPLINE states the perishable-surface mechanism (flash rust, repassivation, dry-out), the wet-fast-staged transfer rule, and the holding-rinse-plus-reactivation response to delays instead of hoping

competency_questions.question: What is the hard segregation line in run handling, and which obligation classes bind every physical act at this bench?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHEMISTRY_SEGREGATION_LINE states that cyanide solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together and never share a drain including rinse waters and travel paths, and HANDLING_SAFETY_OBLIGATIONS names the PPE, ventilation, no-touch, containment and training obligation classes with verify-your-jurisdiction attached

competency_questions.question: What happens between the gold tank and the customer's first look - rinse, dry, unmask, unrack, first touch?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POST_PLATE_RINSE_DRY sequences recovery-first rinsing to a DI final, gentle drying and residue checking, and FIRST_TOUCH_UNRACKING covers glove-handled unracking, contact-mark inspection against the plan and soft-packed handoff to quality

competency_questions.question: What must the run log capture so any result can be reproduced, diagnosed or defended later?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RUN_LOG_DISCIPLINE lists the fields recorded during the run - job, batch, route, fixture id, bath ids, tank order walked, agitation, rinse gates, delays, unrack observations, operator, timestamps - plus the electrical column supplied by the electrical-control work

competency_questions.question: When may jobs share a run, and when must a batch be split no matter what it costs?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BATCH_GROUPING_STRATEGY defines compatibility (same chemistry sequence, same deposit spec, comparable geometry class, same handling class), the one-spec-per-run rule, and the closed area list that refuses late additions

competency_questions.question: How do I execute selective coverage - brush work and masking - without bleed, ghost lines or dishonest thickness claims?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BRUSH_SELECTIVE_ROUTE scopes pen work to repair, accent and non-immersible zones with aliquot, nib and polarity discipline and its flash-to-light-micron honesty limit, and MASKING_STOPOFF_CLASSES covers mask product classes, edge burnishing, sequence compatibility testing and residue-checked removal

competency_questions.question: When has fixturing lost, and what does an honest escalation of an unrackable piece contain?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNRACKABLE_ESCALATION triggers on any piece that cannot be gripped or contacted without unsanctioned damage and produces a documented decision request to intake and the customer - options considered, why each fails, residual risks - never a forced run

glossary.definition: A frame - typically a titanium or stainless spine carrying plastisol-coated copper wiring - that holds pieces individually on hooks, spring clips or wire cradles, enters the tank as one electrical body, and gives the operator per-piece control of orientation, spacing and contact.

The tough plastic coating over a rack's current-carrying members that stops the rack itself from plating; a nick or breach in it becomes an uncounted cathode that steals current from the work and collects gold on the rack, which is why coating checks are per run, not per month.

Plating a mass of small parts inside a slowly rotating perforated drum, current reaching them through internal contacts and part-to-part touch; per-piece labor collapses, but average thickness runs thinner and less uniform than rack work and parts pick up fine contact bruising - a mechanism, not a defect to tune away.

A flexible insulated cathode cable ending in an exposed contact button that rides inside a plating barrel's tumbling load, feeding current into whichever parts touch it; worn dangler insulation or eroded buttons are a classic cause of patchy barrel coverage.

The film of process solution a load carries out of every tank on its surfaces, in its recesses and on the fixture; it is simultaneously lost chemistry (money, when the tank is gold), the physical carrier of cross-tank contamination, and the driver of rinse-water waste.

A static, non-flowing rinse tank placed directly after (or before) a critical tank; positioned after gold it accumulates gold-bearing drag-out as a labeled recovery stream rather than waste, and it buffers the critical bath from what the work carries - at the price of growing steadily more concentrated until it is refreshed.

Two or three rinse tanks plumbed so fresh water enters the last tank and overflows backward against the work's direction of travel; standard rinse-ratio arithmetic makes a cascade dramatically more water-efficient than a single overflow rinse at the same final cleanliness.

A pass/fail check on rinse water quality using a simple conductivity meter before work advances to a critical tank; rising conductivity means accumulated drag-in, and a failed gate stops the transfer rather than letting a contaminated rinse feed the gold bath.

Platers tape, peelable lacquer and wax product classes applied to zones that must not plate or must not meet a chemistry; applied per product instructions with burnished edges against solution creep, tested for compatibility with the tank sequence, and removed with a residue inspection.

The small unplated or thin-plated shadow left where the rack tip, clip or cathode lead touched the piece - current cannot plate its own doorway; the craft is to place it where design hides it, size it so it carries the current without burning, and inspect it at unracking against the contact plan.

nodes.definition: Translate the finished job sheet - the microns target and measurement points from electrical control, the layer stack and its compliance flags from layer architecture - into the plan the hands will execute: candidate route (rack, barrel or brush), tank sequence, which fixture carries the piece, where it will be contacted, what gets masked, and what the log must capture. The plan is written before the first piece is touched because every later choice hangs off it; a run improvised at the tank line cannot be reproduced or defended when the deposit is questioned. Interfaces pass through untouched: setpoints stay with the TDS and the shop log, the stack spec - including any nickel-release compliance flag on skin-contact goods - is copied forward as written with its verify-jurisdiction clause, and any piece the plan cannot fixture without damage is flagged for escalation now, at the desk, not discovered with the piece already activated.

included: written per-job plan naming route, tank order, fixture, contacts and masking
compliance flags copied through from the stack spec
escalation flags raised at planning time
excluded: choosing setpoints (TDS plus the electrical-control KB)

pros.claim: A written run plan makes the physical run auditable end to end
pros.example: when a batch comes back hazy, the plan plus the log shows which rack, which tank order and which rinse gates the load actually saw, so diagnosis starts from facts instead of memory

cons.claim: Planning overhead feels absurd on one-piece jobs and tempts the bench to skip planning entirely
cons.example: a single flash-refresh ring hardly needs a route debate, so the plan must scale down to a one-line entry rather than a form nobody fills

failure_modes: the run is improvised at the tank line and leaves no reproducible record
stack compliance flags are dropped between the job sheet and the bench copy
a fixturing problem surfaces mid-run with the piece already activated instead of at the desk
acceptance_tests: every job entering the line carries a written plan naming route, tank order, fixture, contact zones, masking, and the compliance flags copied from the stack spec
revisit_triggers: the job sheet changes after the plan is written
the planned fixture proves unavailable or unfit at load time

base.update_signal: a defect investigation the written plan plus log could not reconstruct, or a new route or fixture class entering the shop

nodes.definition: Bind every physical act of run handling to its obligation classes before any technique is discussed: gloves and eye protection whenever hands work over open process solutions; ventilation classes over tanks that fume or mist; no-touch handling of activated and freshly plated work - tools and gloved hands, never bare skin; spill trays and secondary containment under everything carried; labeled storage with acids and cyanide-bearing products physically separated; and the hard line that cyanide solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together, and never share a drain - a rule that explicitly covers the rinse waters, drip trays and mop buckets this KB routes, and the path a dripping rack travels across the room. These are obligation classes plus formal-training pointers, never improvised procedure, and every one of them closes with verify your jurisdiction's workplace and hazmat rules. Run handling is where obligations meet hands: the person walking a wet rack between tanks is exactly who the segregation line protects.

included: PPE, ventilation, containment, labeling, storage-separation, no-touch and training obligation classes applied to run handling
the cyanide-acid hard line as it binds transfers, rinses and drains
verify-jurisdiction and formal-training pointers
excluded: emergency medical guidance, which routes to professional care

pros.claim: Naming obligations at run level makes them enforceable at the exact moment of handling
pros.example: the transfer route is drawn so a dripping cyanide-gold rack never passes over the open acid activation tank, because the plan encodes the segregation line as bench geography

cons.claim: Obligation-class language cannot substitute for the formal training it points to
cons.example: a new bench hand who can recite the segregation line still needs supervised training before handling cyanide-bearing gold solutions at all

failure_modes: safety treated as wall posters instead of run-plan content
acid and cyanide lines sharing a rinse bucket or drain under time pressure
bare-hand touching of activated work out of old habit
acceptance_tests: every run plan shows PPE class, transfer path, containment and the segregation line respected, and no acid-line and cyanide-line stream shares a vessel, drain or travel crossing anywhere in the plan
revisit_triggers: a new chemistry class enters the shop
a near-miss, spill or jurisdiction rule change touches any handling obligation

base.update_signal: a jurisdiction rule change, a supplier SDS revision, or any incident or near-miss in run handling

nodes.definition: Decide which jobs may share a run. Compatible means: the same required chemistry sequence, the same deposit spec (color family and thickness class), a comparable geometry class so one current window serves every piece, and the same handling class - a tumble-tolerant lot never shares a plan with a clip-racked pendant. Grouping is the small shop's economics lever, because prep time and tank time amortize over the load, but the governing rule is spec purity: a run has exactly one spec, and pieces are grouped into it; the spec is never bent to fill a tank. The batch list with its piece count and per-piece area class is a closed input the electrical-control amps calculation consumes, so late additions to a racked load are refused once the area estimate is closed - one extra piece silently dilutes current across the whole load. Splitting a batch is always available and always cheaper than replating two specs' worth of wrong pieces.

included: compatibility test across chemistry sequence, deposit spec, geometry class and handling class
one-spec-per-run rule
closed batch list feeding the area estimate
excluded: computing amps from the area list (electrical-control KB)

pros.claim: Batching amortizes the line's fixed time over many pieces without touching quality
pros.example: ten brass charms sharing one flash spec ride one rack, one prep pass and one log entry instead of ten of each

cons.claim: The urge to fill a tank invites spec-mixing that fails every piece in the load at once
cons.example: adding one heavy-build ring to a flash batch either starves the ring against its spec or gilds the charms far past theirs - one run, two failures, paid in gold and rework

failure_modes: mixing thickness classes in one run because the tank had room
adding a piece after the area estimate closed, thinning the whole load
grouping delicate and robust pieces into one handling class to save a rack
acceptance_tests: each run's batch list shows one chemistry sequence, one deposit spec, one geometry class band and one handling class, closed before amps are computed
revisit_triggers: logged runs show a geometry class band was drawn too wide for even coverage
recurring under-filled runs pressure the grouping rules

base.update_signal: a mixed-load defect traced to grouping, or logged evidence that a compatibility band can safely widen or must narrow

nodes.definition: Choose the physical route per piece geometry, batch size, finish class and deposit spec, and record the reason. Rack is the default for show finishes, larger or delicate pieces, heavier builds, and anything whose orientation, spacing and contact must be controlled piece by piece. Barrel earns its place on quantities of small, robust, tumble-tolerant parts - jump rings, clasps, spacer findings - where per-piece labor must vanish and slight part-on-part contact is acceptable. Brush or pen selective work is the repair, accent and post-assembly route: worn-spot re-plates, two-tone detail, one zone of an assembly that cannot be immersed - never whole-piece production, because operator-minutes per piece and its realistic flash-to-light-micron build make brush-only coverage dishonest to sell as micron plating. Boundary cases get a documented test (a sacrifice piece tumbled, a mock-up racked) rather than a guess, and the logged outcomes of past runs are the table this decision is checked against.

included: fitness test per route across geometry, batch size, finish class and deposit spec
recorded decision with reason
documented boundary-case tests
excluded: executing each route (the three route nodes)
current-distribution consequences of the choice (electrical-control KB)

pros.claim: An explicit route decision stops both wasted labor and ruined show pieces
pros.example: a tray of fifty solid jump rings goes to the barrel while the one polished pendant in the same order is clip-racked, each with a one-line stated reason

cons.claim: Boundary cases genuinely resist any fitness table
cons.example: two dozen lightweight hollow charms are uneconomic to rack singly yet dent-prone in a barrel; the honest answer is a tumble test on a sacrifice piece, which costs a piece

failure_modes: routing show-finish pieces to barrel to save racking labor
selling brush-only coverage against a micron-class claim
route chosen by habit with no recorded reason, so failures teach nothing
acceptance_tests: every job's route is recorded with its reason, and any boundary case shows a documented test result rather than an assumption
revisit_triggers: logged outcomes show a route repeatedly failing its class
a new fixture or barrel class changes what a route can economically carry

base.update_signal: route-linked defect or cost patterns in the run log, or new equipment shifting a route's economic boundary

nodes.definition: Execute the rack route: individually held pieces on a frame that enters the tanks as one electrical body. Bench-scale rack classes: titanium or stainless spines with plastisol-coated copper wiring; tips as hooks, spring clips or twisted-wire cradles chosen per piece geometry; every piece hung with deliberate orientation toward the anodes and a contact the current can trust. Racking is where the operator controls what barrel work cannot: which face shows, which recess vents, where the contact hides, how far each piece sits from its neighbor and from the anode. Its price is per-piece labor at load and unload plus a contact mark to manage on every piece. The craft judgment happens before power-on: a load that hangs wrong plates wrong, and no electrical cleverness afterward rescues a piece shadowed by its neighbor or nodding away from the anode on a loose hook.

included: rack and tip class selection per piece geometry
per-piece orientation and hold style
the labor-versus-control tradeoff of racked work

pros.claim: Full per-piece control of orientation, spacing and contact is the rack's whole value
pros.example: a domed pendant hung face-to-anode with its bail hook doubling as the hidden contact plates its show face true and hides its mark where a chain will sit

cons.claim: Per-piece load and unload labor dominates small-part economics
cons.example: forty small charms racked singly cost several times the handling minutes of one barrel cycle, which is exactly why the route decision exists

failure_modes: a loose hook lets the piece rotate mid-run and plate its show face in shadow
clip pressure chosen for grip strength dents thin hollow work
pieces racked at whatever spacing fits rather than the spacing the plan set
revisit_triggers: unrack inspections show orientation drift or clip damage patterns on a rack class

base.update_signal: a new rack or tip class entering the shop, or unrack damage patterns tied to a hold style

nodes.definition: Execute the barrel route: a perforated rotating drum tumbles a mass of small parts through solution while current reaches them through internal contacts - danglers or button contacts - and part-to-part touch. The mechanism dictates both virtues and limits: per-piece labor collapses and all-over coverage happens without fixturing, but each part spends much of the cycle buried in the load carrying little current, so average thickness runs thinner and less uniform per unit of charge than rack work; deposits pick up fine part-on-part bruising unacceptable on mirror finishes; and the load must be sized so parts tumble freely yet keep contact - too small a load loses contact and plates patchily, too full a load tumbles poorly and bruises harder. Excluded by mechanism, not by taste: pieces that tangle (fine chain, open hooks, ear wires), hollow or dent-prone forms, stone-set or assembled work. Rotation speed, load fraction and any plating-media additions come from the barrel equipment's instructions, never improvisation.

included: tumbling-contact mechanism and its thickness and surface consequences
load-sizing and tangle/dent exclusions
equipment-instruction boundary for rotation and media
excluded: amps and thickness estimation for barrel loads (electrical-control KB)
deciding whether barrel is the route (route-decision node)

pros.claim: Per-piece cost collapses on robust small parts with no fixturing at all
pros.example: hundreds of solid jump rings gold-flashed in one barrel cycle against an afternoon of racking them singly

cons.claim: Bruising and thinner, less uniform deposits are built into the mechanism
cons.example: mirror-polished flat tags come out of a barrel micro-scuffed under raking light no matter how gently it turns

failure_modes: fine chain or hooked parts tumbled into a knotted mass that plates as one lump
a load too small to keep part-to-part contact, leaving patchy bare spots
show-finish parts barreled to save time and scrapped for bruising
revisit_triggers: patchy-coverage or bruising complaints tied to barrel lots in the log

base.update_signal: a barrel-lot defect pattern in the log, or new barrel equipment with different load-fraction instructions

nodes.definition: Execute the brush or pen route: the work made cathodic, a solution-wetted anode nib moved constantly over the target zone, deposition only where the wet nib touches - and the motion is the agitation, because a stopped nib burns. Its legitimate jobs at a jewelry bench: re-plating worn high spots without stripping the piece, selective second-color accents, plating one zone of an assembled piece (a solder joint, a clasp tongue) that cannot be immersed, and mixed-material assemblies where immersion would wreck a component. The discipline set: plan the cathode clip on a hidden feature because the clip spot does not plate; pour a working aliquot and never dip a used nib back into stock; keep dedicated nibs and cups per chemistry; rinse first into the gold-recovery cup; verify polarity before every session because a reversed lead strips instead of plates. Honest scope per the corpus: flash-to-light-micron builds - brush-only coverage is never sold under a micron-plating claim.

included: repair, accent, and non-immersible-zone jobs
aliquot, nib, clip and polarity discipline
flash-to-light-micron honesty limit on claims
excluded: voltage window numbers, which live in the product TDS

pros.claim: It is the only route for zones that cannot be immersed
pros.example: the worn clasp tongue on an assembled bracelet is pen-plated in place without dunking the whole piece and its non-metal components

cons.claim: Operator-minutes per zone and a sub-micron realistic build cap what the route may promise
cons.example: whole-ring coverage by pen takes minutes of skilled constant motion and still cannot honestly carry a micron-class thickness claim

failure_modes: a stopped or dry nib scorching a black mark that must be stripped and re-prepped
a used nib dipped back into the stock bottle, poisoning it
the clip placed on a show surface, leaving an unplated shadow in plain sight
acceptance_tests: each brush job shows a planned hidden clip point, a dedicated-per-chemistry nib and cup, a poured working aliquot, a polarity check, and a first rinse into the recovery cup
revisit_triggers: color-match drift between pen repairs and tank-plated fields in inspection results
a new pen chemistry class arrives with different handling per its TDS

base.update_signal: logged pen-repair outcomes shifting the route's honest scope, or supplier TDS changes to pen chemistry handling

nodes.definition: Control where deposit and chemistry may not go. Platers tape, peelable stop-off lacquer and wax classes mask zones for two-tone work, protect zones the spec excludes, and hold the boundary of selective work at a design line. Masking materials are products applied per their instructions: adhesion proven on the actual pre-plate surface, edges burnished down so solution cannot creep underneath, and compatibility with the whole tank sequence verified - a lacquer that shrugs off a room-temperature gold can lift in a hot cleaner two tanks earlier. Removal is part of the plan, not an afterthought: mask residue left in a recess reads later as a stain or an adhesion killer for any subsequent coat, so removal and residue inspection are logged steps. Boundaries are placed on natural design lines - grooves, edges, steps - where a faint transition disappears; a mask line across an open polished field is visible at arm's length and should be renegotiated at planning. And masking minutes are quoted minutes: the effort is real and belongs in the price, not absorbed as a surprise.

included: mask product classes and where each serves
edge burnishing and sequence-compatibility testing
residue-checked removal as a logged step
boundary placement on design lines
excluded: which zones the spec excludes (job sheet and layer-architecture plan)
mask product chemistry (per its own instructions)

pros.claim: Masking makes selective coverage repeatable on tank runs, not just under a pen
pros.example: a two-tone pendant masked with peelable lacquer along its recessed groove comes out with a crisp boundary the eye reads as designed rather than plated

cons.claim: Creep, lift and residue add three whole failure families to a run
cons.example: solution wicking under a lazily burnished tape edge leaves a feathered ghost line the customer spots instantly on the polished field

failure_modes: mask lifting mid-sequence in a tank it was never tested against
residue left in a recess staining the piece or killing a later coat's adhesion
a mask boundary drawn across an open field where any line shows
revisit_triggers: a masking product change or a tank-sequence change invalidating past compatibility tests

base.update_signal: a masking failure traced in the log, or a new stop-off product class with different compatibility

nodes.definition: Choose where metal touches metal, because every contact point is simultaneously the only doorway current has into the piece and a small unplated or thin shadow on it. The craft: put contacts on hidden features - inside a bail, under a clasp tongue, on a post a finding will cover - and use design features as contacts where the geometry offers them. Then size the contact to the current: a needle-fine hidden touch that cannot carry the load's amps heats, burns the deposit around it or opens intermittently, which is worse than an honest visible mark. Where no hidden point exists, the fallbacks run in order: move the contact mid-run in a second session so each spot gets covered by the other; contact on a zone already scheduled for brush touch-up; or escalate the geometry to the customer decision path. Contact style is also chosen with unracking in mind - fresh plate is soft and clip jaws scar it on the way off - and the whole choice is written per piece class in the contact plan, never improvised at the rack.

included: hidden-feature contact preference and design-feature contacts
contact sized to the current it must carry
ordered fallbacks: mid-run move, touch-up zone, escalation
written per-piece-class contact plan
excluded: how much current the load draws (electrical-control KB)

pros.claim: A well-placed, well-sized contact makes the mark vanish into the design
pros.example: hooking a pendant through its bail puts the mark on the inside curve where the hanging chain covers it for the life of the piece

cons.claim: The best-hidden spots are often the worst current paths
cons.example: contacting inside a fine bail on a heavy build concentrates the load's amps in a wire-thin touch that heats, steps the deposit and can spark black at entry

failure_modes: a contact mark discovered on a display face at unracking because nobody planned the point
a tiny hidden contact burning or opening intermittently under the load's current
clip jaws sized for grip scarring the fresh deposit at unload
acceptance_tests: every racked piece class has a written contact plan naming the point, why it is hidden or sanctioned, and that it carries the planned current without heating; pieces with no workable point show a fallback or an escalation flag
revisit_triggers: unrack inspection finds marks outside planned zones
the electrical plan changes the current the contact must carry

base.update_signal: unrack contact-map results contradicting the plan, or a new tip class changing what a hidden point can carry

nodes.definition: Trust the rack only after checking it, every run: continuity from the rectifier bus to every tip; the spine connection tight; plastisol coating unbroken, because a breach becomes an uncounted cathode that plates the rack, steals current from the work and silently grows the load's true area; tips clean of plated buildup that spoils contact; spring tension still gripping. The check is per run, not per month, because rack condition drifts with every strip cycle and every drop. Whatever bare rack metal and robbers the check finds are reported into the area facts the electrical-control calculation consumes - an unreported breach is an area error wearing a maintenance costume. All rigging stays within the rack and rectifier manufacturer's instructions: no improvised splices, no undersized leads, and mains-side work goes to a qualified electrician, full stop.

included: per-run continuity, coating, tip and spring checks
exposed-metal and robber reporting to the area facts
equipment-instruction boundary on rigging

pros.claim: A two-minute rack check catches the invisible failure class before it spends gold
pros.example: a hairline plastisol breach found at check would otherwise have gold-plated the spine while every charm on the rack came out thin against spec

cons.claim: Check discipline erodes exactly when racks cycle hardest
cons.example: the chipped tip slips through on the Friday rush, which is why the check lives as a gate in the workflow rather than a habit in someone's head

failure_modes: a coating breach plating the rack and thinning the whole load
an open tip leaving one piece bare while its rack-mates plate
buildup on tips making contacts intermittent and deposits stepped
acceptance_tests: before each run the fixture check record shows continuity to every tip, coating intact or the breach quantified into the area facts, and tips clean and gripping
revisit_triggers: a defect investigation traces to fixture condition
a new rack class changes what the per-run check must cover

base.update_signal: a fixture-traced defect, or a rack class whose failure pattern the current check misses

nodes.definition: Position pieces so each one sees solution and current honestly: spacing wide enough that neighbors do not shadow each other into starved zones; show faces toward the anodes; geometry kept consistent across the rack so one current window serves every piece; awareness that outer rack positions ride the field edge and plate heavier than the crowded middle; and the loaded area held to what the plan's amps assumed. Overcrowding is the classic throughput temptation and it fails arithmetically: each extra piece dilutes current per unit area across the whole load, shadows its neighbors, and drags every piece toward the thin end of spec at once. The loaded rack is compared against the plan before it enters any tank - count, positions, orientation - because repositioning after the first chemistry means re-prepping the work, and a photograph of the loaded rack is the cheapest load record a small shop can keep.

included: neighbor-shadowing and spacing discipline
anode facing and field-edge awareness
load held to the closed area estimate
pre-tank load-versus-plan comparison
excluded: current-distribution prediction and mitigation hardware (electrical-control KB)

pros.claim: Honest spacing buys more uniformity than any downstream correction
pros.example: opening the gap between two flat charms erases the pale kissing-shadow stripe each was printing on the other, with no shielding hardware involved

cons.claim: Honest spacing costs load size and therefore run count
cons.example: the same order at plan spacing takes two racks instead of one, and the schedule feels it - which is the pressure the dominance rule exists to answer

failure_modes: overcrowding thinning the entire load below spec
a piece hung with its show face angled off-anode plating dull on the side that matters
field-edge outer pieces over-plating while middle pieces starve in a packed rack
revisit_triggers: thickness results split by rack position in the log
a load photographed at variance with its plan

base.update_signal: position-correlated thickness patterns in logged runs, or a rack redesign changing usable positions

nodes.definition: Orient each piece so gas escapes and solution drains, because geometry seals what agitation cannot reach. A cupped or domed feature hung mouth-up traps hydrogen and air as a pocket that plates nothing - a bald spot ringed by a tide line; hung mouth-down it traps solution that rides to the next tank as concentrated drag-out and later bleeds out of seams to stain the dried piece. The craft is tilt: hollows angled so bubbles vent along an edge where the tide line hides in the design, and so solution sheets off a low point; bail holes and tube features positioned to flush in the rinse; blind recesses flagged in the plan for extra drain dwell and a directed rinse. Venting and drainage are decided at racking time - once the piece is under power, the pocket is plating its absence into the deposit, and no post-hoc agitation reliably clears a pocket the geometry sealed.

included: tilt discipline for venting and drainage
flagging blind recesses for dwell and directed rinse
tide-line placement on design edges

pros.claim: A small tilt at racking prevents whole defect families downstream
pros.example: a domed pendant angled slightly off vertical vents its bubble along the rim where the faint tide line disappears into the design edge instead of the dome's center

cons.claim: Ideal venting and ideal anode facing can disagree on the same piece
cons.example: the tilt that vents a dome turns its face partly off-anode; the resolution costs either an auxiliary-anode conversation with electrical control or an accepted thinner class on the back face, and the plan must say which

failure_modes: a gas pocket printing a bald spot in the one place the customer looks
a solution-filled cup carrying concentrated chemistry into the next tank
a blind recess bleeding stain onto a dried, finished piece hours later
revisit_triggers: recurring tide lines or crevice stains on a piece class in inspection results

base.update_signal: a hollow or cupped piece class entering the shop, or stain and bald-spot patterns tied to orientation in the log

nodes.definition: Deliver fresh solution to every working surface. Bench-scale agitation classes: cathode-rod movement that sways the rack itself; pumped solution and eductors; filtered recirculation; air sparging - with the corpus-backed flag that air-agitating nickel-bearing tanks throws mist whose inhalable nickel is a carcinogen-class exposure, so mist control or a non-air class is the rule there; barrel rotation for the barrel route; and in brush work the nib's constant motion, which is why a stopped nib burns. What agitation does is mechanism: it thins the depleted solution layer at the work face and raises the burn threshold - the limiting-current interface owned by electrical control - and what it cannot do is reach a sealed pocket or substitute for spacing. Hardware runs per its equipment instructions; the run plan names the agitation class per tank and the log records that it actually ran, because a batch plated with the pump silently off is a different batch than the one planned.

included: agitation class per tank and per route
mist-control flag on air-agitated nickel-bearing tanks
planned-versus-ran verification in the log
excluded: bath chemistry responses to agitation (bath-chemistry specialist)

pros.claim: Matching agitation class to tank and route removes a silent variable from every run
pros.example: switching a small gold tank from still to gentle cathode-rod motion evens out the streaky thin patches that appeared whenever loads got dense

cons.claim: Agitation flatters overcrowding without fixing it
cons.example: turning the pump up lets a packed rack pass one run and fail the next, hiding the spacing problem the plan should have caught

failure_modes: air-agitating a nickel-bearing tank with no mist control
the planned pump found off mid-run with no note in the log
trusting agitation to clear a sealed pocket that only re-orientation clears
revisit_triggers: streaky or position-dependent deposits appearing when load density rises
an equipment change altering which agitation classes a tank supports

base.update_signal: deposit patterns correlated with agitation state in the log, or new agitation hardware with different instructions

nodes.definition: Manage the film of solution every load carries out of every tank - the shop's simultaneous money leak, contamination vector and waste driver. The levers: withdraw slowly, because a racing exit carries a thicker film; dwell over the tank with the rack tilted so solution sheets back from a low corner; give cupped features their documented tip-and-drain move; and let drip bars catch what travel would scatter. Direction matters to what the film means: after the gold tank, drag-out is value, so the first stop is the dead recovery rinse where it accumulates as a labeled reclaim stream instead of waste; before the gold tank, drag-out of the previous chemistry is the poison the rinse sequence exists to remove. Gold-bearing drag-out, rinses and spent aliquots are labeled recovery streams routed to reclaim - never a drain - a regulated-class routing verified per jurisdiction. The recovery cup and dead rinse are where a small shop's gold economics quietly live or die.

included: withdrawal speed, dwell, tilt and drip control
recovery-first routing after gold
labeled reclaim streams with jurisdiction verification

pros.claim: Dwell and recovery discipline turn an invisible loss into a measured stream
pros.example: the dead rinse ahead of reclaim accumulates gold that would have left on the work and in the wastewater, and its assay tells the shop what its handling habits cost

cons.claim: Dwell fights the transfer clock on perishable surfaces
cons.example: holding an activated-nickel load over the rinse to drain is exactly the delay that lets the surface passivate; the conflict is resolved by rule, not by mood

failure_modes: racing loads out of gold and paying for it in the reclaim assay
cupped features dumping concentrated chemistry into the next tank
gold-bearing rinse water treated as waste and lost down a sanctioned drain
revisit_triggers: reclaim assay or rinse-conductivity trends showing drag-out rising
a new piece class that holds solution in ways current dwell practice misses

base.update_signal: reclaim assay results, rising rinse conductivity, or a jurisdiction change on reclaim stream handling

nodes.definition: Design the water between the tanks. The standard classes: counterflow cascade rinses - two or three tanks with fresh water flowing against the work's direction - which standard rinse-ratio arithmetic makes dramatically more water-efficient than one big overflow rinse; a dead rinse directly ahead of the gold tank that both catches gold drag-out for recovery and buffers the gold bath from what the work carries in; conductivity gates before critical tanks, run with a cheap conductivity meter, where a failed reading stops the transfer; and DI or RO water for final rinses because tap chloride and hardness spot the work and poison sensitive baths. The sequence also encodes its exceptions: silicated cleaner carry-over gels in acid, so silicate lines get a hot double rinse; and some strike-to-plate transfers are deliberately not rinsed, or rinsed minimally, per the product's TDS to beat repassivation - the sequence follows the product instructions, not a universal rule. Every rinse has a named identity - which chemistry line it serves - because an anonymous rinse bucket is how acid and cyanide streams end up meeting.

included: counterflow cascade and dead-rinse placement
conductivity gates that stop transfers
DI final rinses
named rinse identity per chemistry line
TDS-driven no-rinse exceptions

pros.claim: A designed rinse sequence protects the most expensive tank in the shop for the price of plumbing and a meter
pros.example: the dead rinse plus a two-stage cascade ahead of gold keeps nickel and chloride drag-in - both listed poisons of gold chemistry in the corpus - from ever reaching the bath

cons.claim: More rinse stages mean more tanks, more floor space and more water discipline
cons.example: a cramped bench that cannot fit a third cascade tank must compensate with longer dwell and tighter conductivity gates, and the sequence doc must say so

failure_modes: one overflow rinse doing every job and slowly poisoning the gold bath
a conductivity gate skipped because the meter was across the room
rinsing a strike surface the TDS said to transfer wet and unrinsed
an unlabeled rinse serving two chemistry lines
acceptance_tests: the line diagram shows every rinse's identity and direction of flow, a dead rinse ahead of gold, conductivity gates at critical entries with stop authority, and DI final rinses; TDS-driven no-rinse exceptions are written on the diagram
revisit_triggers: gold-bath analysis shows drag-in contamination climbing
a chemistry change adds or removes a rinse-sensitive transfer
conductivity gate failures becoming frequent at one station

base.update_signal: gold-bath contamination trends, a plumbing or layout change, or a product TDS altering a transfer's rinse requirement

nodes.definition: Run the clock between tanks, because several surfaces in this trade are perishable: bare steel flash-rusts in air within a minute-class window, activated nickel repassivates within a minutes-class window and then peels its gold, and any dry-out between tanks prints a mark into the deposit. The discipline: transfers are wet and fast; the receiving tank is staged and verified ready before the piece leaves the previous one; the line is walked in one direction with no doubling back over open tanks; and when a delay strikes - a rectifier fault, a phone call, a spill - the piece goes into a holding rinse and its surface is re-activated per the upstream product's instructions rather than hoped over. Priority is by rule: the transfer clock beats drain dwell wherever the receiving surface is perishable, and dwell wins at the gold exit where the next stop is a recovery rinse and the fresh deposit is noble. Staging is the quiet half of the skill - the operator who sets up the next tank before lifting the rack never has to choose between a drip and a peel.

included: wet-fast transfer rule with staged receiving tanks
one-direction line walking
holding-rinse-plus-reactivation response to delays
clock-versus-dwell priority rule
excluded: reactivation chemistry itself (surface-prep specialist per product TDS)

pros.claim: Staging the receiving tank removes the delay class that causes most adhesion escapes
pros.example: verifying the gold tank ready before lifting the nickel-plated load out of its rinse means the activated surface is airborne for seconds, not minutes

cons.claim: A hard transfer clock makes solo operation of a long line genuinely difficult
cons.example: one operator cannot stage tank five while racking tank two, so the plan must batch transfers or accept holding-rinse pauses - pretending otherwise is how pieces strand

failure_modes: an activated surface stranded in air while the operator troubleshoots something else
flash rust blooming on steel between tanks and getting plated over
doubling back over open tanks with a dripping rack
a delayed piece pushed onward without reactivation because the schedule hurt
acceptance_tests: every transfer in the plan names its receiving tank staged-and-verified step, and the delay response (holding rinse plus reactivation per product instructions) is written where the operator stands
revisit_triggers: adhesion failures clustered on runs with logged delays
line layout changes that alter walking distance between tanks

base.update_signal: delay-correlated adhesion failures in the log, or a layout or staffing change that alters the achievable clock

nodes.definition: Keep chemistries out of each other, at two severities. The life-safety line first: cyanide-bearing solutions - many golds and some strikes - and acids are never mixed, never stored together, and never share a drain, because acid contact with cyanide generates hydrogen cyanide gas; the rule covers rinse waters, drip trays, mop buckets, spill paths and the route a dripping rack travels, and it admits no convenience exception ever. Below it, the quality segregation that keeps deposits honest: dedicated fixtures, nibs, cups and rinses per chemistry class; nickel-touched tools never dipped toward gold; a rack that visited the stripping line rinsed demonstrably clean before it carries plating work again. Segregation is physical - bench geography with acids on one side, cyanide products on the other, separated storage, separate spill paths - and procedural: labeling, color-coding, one-way workflows. All of it is obligation-class content pointing to formal training and jurisdiction rules; none of it is improvised.

included: the cyanide-acid never-mix never-store never-share-drain line applied to run handling
dedicated-equipment quality segregation per chemistry
physical bench geography and procedural labeling
excluded: cyanide destruct and waste treatment (waste-handling KB)
emergency response procedure, which is formal-training territory

pros.claim: A physically encoded line does not depend on anyone's good day
pros.example: when the acid station and the cyanide-gold station cannot share a drain because the plumbing does not connect, the worst mistake available is a quality fault, not a gas event

cons.claim: Full duplication of fixtures, cups and rinses per chemistry costs real money and bench space
cons.example: a one-bench shop must buy and store parallel nib sets, cups and rinse vessels it uses twice a month - and must anyway, because the alternative is the hazard

failure_modes: an acid rinse and a cyanide rinse sharing a bucket or a drain under time pressure
one nib or cup serving two chemistries and poisoning both
a stripped rack carried straight back to the plating line unrinsed
acceptance_tests: the bench map shows acids and cyanide-bearing products with separated storage, separate spill paths and no shared drain; every fixture, nib, cup and rinse carries a chemistry-line identity; the transfer routes never cross a dripping load over the other line
revisit_triggers: any new chemistry entering the shop
a layout change touching storage, plumbing or travel paths
an audit or near-miss finding against segregation

base.update_signal: a new chemistry, a layout change, a jurisdiction rule change, or any segregation near-miss

nodes.definition: Close the wet phase without wrecking the finish. Out of the gold slowly, so the film stays thin; into the recovery rinse first, because that film is gold; then through clean rinses to a DI final, because tap-water minerals dry into spots on a mirror surface. Dry with warm air or by wicking with a soft cloth - never rubbing, because the fresh deposit is soft. Hollow and creviced pieces get directed flushing and extra drying time: trapped rinse water bleeds out of seams hours later and stains a finished piece, and on cyanide-type chemistry any dried-on electrolyte is not merely cosmetic - residue on a wearable item is a safety and corrosion fault the corpus names, so the dried piece must pass the shop's residue check (a neutral-wipe class inspection). Masking comes off per its product instructions with a residue inspection of its own. Nothing touches bare skin until the piece is rinsed, dried and checked - the handoff to first-touch handling starts clean or not at all.

included: recovery-first exit from gold
DI final rinse and gentle drying
directed flushing and extended drying for hollows
residue check on wearables
mask removal with residue inspection
excluded: reclaim processing of the recovery stream (waste-handling KB)

pros.claim: A disciplined close protects everything the tanks just paid for
pros.example: the same batch that survives strike, nickel and gold perfectly can still be scrapped by hard-water spots from one lazy final rinse - the DI final costs pennies against that

cons.claim: Hollow pieces stretch drying time far past what the schedule expects
cons.example: a locket-class piece needs directed flushing and a warm-air dwell long after its solid rack-mates are boxed, and rushing it trades minutes now for a stain claim later

failure_modes: dried-on electrolyte residue on a wearable item
hard-water spotting from a tap final rinse
crevice bleed staining a piece after it was boxed
rubbing a fresh soft deposit into hairline scuffs while drying
revisit_triggers: stain, spot or residue findings at inspection tied to the close-out steps

base.update_signal: residue or spotting findings at inspection, or a water-quality change at the final rinse

nodes.definition: The first human touch after plating decides whether the bench keeps what the tanks made. Fresh gold is soft and often thin: clips are opened without dragging their jaws across the face, pieces come off over a soft surface so a slip is a bounce and not a ding, and hands wear gloves or finger cots because skin oils print visibly into a thin flash. Unracking is also the inspection moment for the contact plan: is each mark inside its planned hidden zone, does any need brush touch-up, and does the pattern match the plan - a mark where none was planned means a piece rotated or shifted mid-run, which is a racking lesson worth capturing in the log. Pieces then go into soft trays or bags, segregated so they cannot scratch each other, and the lot is released to the quality specialist with its contact map, so the person measuring thickness knows not to gauge on a contact shadow and the person judging color knows which zones were pen-touched.

included: glove and soft-surface unracking technique
contact-mark inspection against the plan
touch-up routing
soft-packed handoff with the contact map

pros.claim: Inspecting contacts at unracking closes the loop on the contact plan the same day
pros.example: a mark found outside its planned zone traces to a loose hook within the hour, and the next load hangs on a fixed tip instead of repeating the flaw

cons.claim: Careful unracking is slow exactly when the batch feels finished
cons.example: the last five minutes of a flawless run is when a hurried thumb prints a matte oval into a mirror flash - the handling rule has to outlast the operator's patience

failure_modes: fingerprints etched into thin flash by bare-hand handling
clip jaws scarring the deposit on the way off
finished pieces tumbled together in one tray scratching each other
the lot handed to quality without its contact map
revisit_triggers: handling-damage findings at final inspection
quality reporting measurements taken on contact shadows for lack of a map

base.update_signal: handling-damage patterns at inspection, or a piece class whose unracking needs a new technique

nodes.definition: Tie every job to its parameters, during the run, not from memory at closing time. The fields: job id and batch list; route and the decision reason; fixture id; bath ids; the tank order actually walked; the electrical column supplied by the electrical-control work - amps, minutes, area estimate - logged here, owned there; agitation class per tank and whether it ran; rinse gates passed with their conductivity readings; drain-dwell exceptions; masking on and off; transfer delays and the reactivations they triggered; unrack observations and the contact-map result; operator and timestamps. The log is the shop's evidence base: it makes 'we did what the plan said' a checkable fact, turns a defect into a diagnosis - which tank, which rack, which delay - feeds the fixture-linked maintenance record, refines route and dwell policy over time, and backs every claim the business side makes about the job. A run that is not logged effectively did not happen: it cannot be reproduced, defended, or learned from.

included: the run-log field set recorded during the run
log as diagnosis, reproduction and defense instrument
fixture-linked and route-linked learning loops

pros.claim: A during-the-run log converts every defect into tuition instead of mystery
pros.example: a peeling batch traced through the log to a twenty-minute logged delay before gold - with the reactivation step absent - fixes the delay response for every future run

cons.claim: Logging competes with wet hands at the worst moments
cons.example: the operator mid-transfer cannot write, so the log design needs check-boxes, pre-filled plans and a pencil at each station or it will be reconstructed - badly - at five o'clock

failure_modes: the log reconstructed from memory at day's end
the electrical column missing because each side assumed the other logged it
exceptions (delays, dwell changes, gate failures) happening but never written
logs kept but never read back into route and dwell policy
acceptance_tests: a randomly picked past job can be fully reconstructed from its log - route, fixture, baths, tank order, electrical column, gates, exceptions, operator - without asking anyone
revisit_triggers: a defect investigation stalls on a missing field
a new route, fixture class or gate adds a field the log lacks

base.update_signal: an investigation blocked by a missing log field, or workflow changes adding parameters worth capturing

nodes.definition: Fixtures age with every cycle, and their aging is a quality variable. Rack tips accumulate plate that must be stripped - per the stripping product's instructions, in its own segregated line, with the stripped gold flagged as a recovery stream; plastisol develops nicks that plate and steal current; spring contacts fatigue and lose grip; barrel danglers wear their insulation and erode their buttons; brush nibs and covers load with chemistry and are consumables with a per-chemistry identity, never shared. The lifecycle discipline: an inspection and stripping cadence per fixture class driven by cycle count; a tagged retirement path for fixtures beyond economic repair; fixture identity carried in the run log so a bad fixture's history is traceable across runs. The cadence is set by evidence, not virtue: a shop that never maintains pays through misplated loads, one that over-maintains pays in strip chemistry and labor, and the log's fixture-linked defect record is what says which side of that line the shop is on.

included: stripping, repair and retirement cadence per fixture class
consumable identity for nibs and covers
fixture-linked defect tracing through the log
stripped gold as a recovery stream
excluded: stripping chemistry selection (per product instructions and bath-chemistry counsel)

pros.claim: Cycle-driven maintenance catches fixture decay before the per-run check has to
pros.example: stripping rack tips on cadence keeps contact resistance predictable, so the per-run check finds surprises rarely instead of weekly

cons.claim: Maintenance consumes chemistry, labor and fixture downtime
cons.example: a small shop's only long rack out for strip-and-repair on a busy day forces a schedule choice the cadence should have anticipated

failure_modes: tips stripped never, until loads misplate
a fatigued spring clip dropping a piece into a tank mid-run
nibs shared across chemistries to save consumable cost
no fixture id in the log, so a bad rack's history is invisible
revisit_triggers: fixture-linked defects recurring inside the current cadence
a new fixture class with unknown aging behavior entering service

base.update_signal: fixture-linked defect trends in the log, or reclaim value from stripping shifting the cadence economics

nodes.definition: Know when fixturing has lost. Some pieces cannot be racked, clipped, wired or cradled without damage the customer never sanctioned: micro-thin hollow forms that any spring pressure dents; closed forms with no hidden feature to contact; assemblies whose only contactable zones are display faces; pieces whose coating or repair history makes every candidate grip a risk. The boundary rule is absolute: such a piece is escalated to intake and the customer decision path with the attempted options documented - which contact zones were considered and why each fails, whether a two-session contact move or the brush route could serve, and what residual risk each option carries - and it is never forced onto the line to keep a schedule. The escalation output is a decision request, not a refusal: the customer may accept a stated visible mark location, accept a brush-only partial service honestly scoped to its flash-class limits, or decline the work. The one option never on the menu is improvising a grip and hoping.

included: triggers that end the fixturing attempt
documented options-considered record
decision-request handoff to intake and customer
honest scoping of any brush-only fallback
excluded: the intake conversation and liability documentation (client-intake specialist)

pros.claim: A hard escalation boundary converts a probable damage event into a documented customer choice
pros.example: a paper-thin antique locket that any clip would dent goes back to intake with three scoped options instead of coming off the rack with a crease no apology fixes

cons.claim: Escalation costs turnaround time and sometimes the job itself
cons.example: the customer who hears 'we need your decision on a visible mark' may take the piece elsewhere - and that outcome is still cheaper than the dented locket

failure_modes: an improvised grip denting or scarring an irreplaceable piece
escalation raised only after damage, as an explanation instead of a question
a brush-only fallback sold without its flash-class honesty limits
acceptance_tests: every escalated piece shows the options-considered record (zones, failures, fallbacks, residual risks) and a customer decision captured before any further handling
revisit_triggers: a new fixture class makes a previously unrackable geometry holdable
an escalated-piece pattern suggesting the boundary triggers fire too early or too late

base.update_signal: a damage event on a piece that should have escalated, or a fixture innovation moving the boundary

edges.why_related: batches are composed from jobs whose plans state their spec, route candidate and handling class
the route decision executes the plan's candidate route against the fitness test
batch size is one of the route decision's inputs - quantity is what makes barrel thinkable
rack execution begins only after the route decision selects it with a reason
barrel execution begins only after the route decision selects it with a reason
brush work begins only when the route decision scopes it to repair, accent or non-immersible zones
the chosen route and coverage plan determine what must be masked and against which tank sequence
contact planning works with the tip and hold classes the rack route provides
pen work needs the same hidden-contact planning for its cathode clip, which leaves an unplated spot
the rack chosen for the run is the rack the per-run electrical check must certify
pieces are hung on their planned contacts first; spacing and facing are arranged around those holds
venting tilt is applied within the spacing and anode-facing arrangement already set
what can drain at the tank lip is decided by how the piece was oriented at racking
the rinse sequence is sized against the drag-out load the withdrawal and dwell discipline leaves behind
the transfer clock runs across the rinse stations and gates the sequence defines
the close-out rinse chain (recovery, cascade, DI final) is the tail of the designed sequence
unracking starts only on a rinsed, dried, residue-checked piece
per-run check findings are the raw evidence the maintenance cadence is set from
the segregation line is the sharpest of the handling obligation classes, applied to routes, rinses and drains
the log's field set mirrors the plan - each planned choice becomes a recorded fact
escalation triggers when the contact plan exhausts its ordered fallbacks without a safe option
air agitation of nickel-bearing tanks requires mist control or a non-air class; agitation hardware stays within its equipment instructions
pen work holds open solution inches from the hand, so PPE, tray, ventilation and segregation obligations bind every session
rinse identity per chemistry line and the no-shared-drain rule are non-negotiable inputs to the sequence design
the load may not exceed what the certified tips and wiring can carry, whatever spacing would fit
mask removal with residue inspection is a mandatory step inside the close-out sequence when masking was used
no-touch and glove obligations govern the first-touch moment, when bare skin is most tempted
drain dwell over the tank and the transfer clock pull the same seconds in opposite directions
edges.resolution_rule: where the receiving surface is perishable (activated nickel, struck steel), the transfer clock wins and the dead rinse captures what dwell would have; at the gold exit the dwell wins, because the deposit is noble and the next stop is the recovery rinse

edges.why_related: filling a barrel or rack argues for widening the batch, while route fitness argues for splitting it
edges.resolution_rule: spec and route purity win: a piece is never re-routed to an unfit process or merged into an incompatible batch to fill a load; an under-filled run is a pricing problem for the business side, not a fixturing decision

edges.why_related: the most invisible contact point and the most current-capable contact path are often different points
edges.resolution_rule: the contact must carry the planned current without heating or intermittence; if no hidden point can, use a mid-run contact move or a planned brush touch-up zone, and if neither serves, escalate - a starving contact is never run

edges.why_related: pen work's small cups, nibs and clips invite convenient sharing across chemistries at one crowded bench
edges.resolution_rule: segregation always wins: dedicated nibs, cups and vessels per chemistry, acids physically separated from cyanide-type solutions, no shared rinse or drain - convenience is never a reason, and the cost of duplication is part of offering pen service

edges.why_related: undrained crevice solution set at racking re-emerges as bleed stains during and after drying
dense loading shadows solution flow between neighbors, raising the agitation demand the tank must meet
maintenance findings and cadence results tune what the per-run check looks for on each fixture class
contact-mark inspection at unracking routes touch-up work back into the pen route's queue
logged route outcomes are the evidence the route fitness table is corrected against
logged reclaim assays and rinse-gate readings tune the withdrawal and dwell policy
masking is applied and cured before pieces are racked; a mask applied on the rack is a mask applied badly
the last timed transfer of the run delivers the work into the close-out rinse chain
both are immersion tank routes sharing live-contact requirements and the same rinse and transfer discipline, differing in per-piece control versus bulk economics

conflict_axes.name: throughput_vs_per_piece_control
conflict_axes.description: Barrel and batch economics push work toward bulk handling while finish class and piece safety pull toward per-piece racked control.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the route fitness test decides per job: finish class, tangle and dent risk, and deposit spec override per-piece cost; barrel only what the mechanism provably tolerates

conflict_axes.name: hidden_contact_vs_current_capacity
conflict_axes.description: The most invisible contact point is often too small or too thin a path to carry the load's current honestly.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: current capacity is the floor: within it, hide the mark; when no hidden point clears the floor, move the contact mid-run, plan a touch-up zone, or escalate - never run a starving contact

conflict_axes.name: load_fill_vs_spacing_honesty
conflict_axes.description: Every empty rack position argues for one more piece, and every added piece dilutes current and shadows a neighbor.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the closed area estimate is the line: load to the plan, split the batch when it does not fit, and let the business side price under-filled runs

conflict_axes.name: drain_dwell_vs_transfer_clock
conflict_axes.description: Seconds spent draining over a tank are seconds an activated surface spends perishing in air.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: rule, not judgment: clock wins over perishable surfaces with the dead rinse catching the loss; dwell wins at the gold exit where the deposit is noble

conflict_axes.name: water_thrift_vs_rinse_purity
conflict_axes.description: Rinse water and stages cost money and space, while insufficient rinsing carries each chemistry into the next tank.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: counterflow cascades give purity and thrift at once; conductivity gates convert the argument into a reading, and a failed gate stops the line

conflict_axes.name: recovery_hoarding_vs_rinse_function
conflict_axes.description: The dead rinse gains reclaim value as it concentrates - and loses buffering function as it does, until it contaminates what passes through it.
poles: refresh it while it still rinses
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: monitor its conductivity like any gate: refresh on reading, send the spent charge to reclaim, and never let the recovery stream become a contamination source

conflict_axes.name: masking_effort_vs_boundary_risk
conflict_axes.description: Every masked edge costs applied minutes and every unmasked or lazily burnished edge risks creep, ghost lines and residue.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: mask to the design line, burnish every edge, test compatibility on a coupon, and put the minutes in the quote instead of skipping them at the bench

conflict_axes.name: schedule_pressure_vs_escalation_honesty
conflict_axes.description: A due date argues for improvising a grip on a difficult piece; the piece's irreversibility argues for stopping and asking.
poles: force a fixture and keep the schedule
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: irreversibility wins: a piece that cannot be held without unsanctioned damage goes to the customer decision path with options documented, and the schedule absorbs it

conflict_axes.name: bench_convenience_vs_segregation
conflict_axes.description: Shared cups, shared rinses, one handy drain and a shortcut path across the room are all conveniences the segregation line forbids.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the cyanide-acid line admits no exception at any severity; below it, dedicated equipment per chemistry is bought as part of offering the service, not debated per run

conflict_axes.name: log_detail_vs_bench_speed
conflict_axes.description: Wet hands cannot write, and unwritten runs cannot be diagnosed - the log competes with the work it records.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: design the log for wet hands - pre-filled plans, check-boxes, a pencil at each station - so recording costs seconds, and never reconstruct from memory

edge_cases.description: A cupped pendant hung mouth-up traps an air pocket and comes out with a bald spot ringed by a tide line
edge_cases.trigger: hollow or cupped geometry racked without venting tilt
edge_cases.mitigation: re-rack with the tilt that vents along a design edge, re-prep, and add the piece class to the venting flag list in the plan

edge_cases.description: A flat charm has display faces on both sides and no hidden feature to contact
edge_cases.trigger: geometry offering no concealable contact point
edge_cases.mitigation: plan a two-session run moving the contact between sessions, or obtain the customer's sanction for a stated mark location; if neither serves, escalate with the options documented

edge_cases.description: A load of fine chain tumbled in the barrel knots into a mass that plates as one lump
edge_cases.trigger: tangle-prone pieces routed to barrel by batch-size pressure
edge_cases.mitigation: route chain and open-hook pieces to rack fixtures regardless of quantity; the tangle exclusion is mechanical, not negotiable by lot size

edge_cases.description: A hairline plastisol breach plates the rack spine with gold while every piece on the rack runs thin
edge_cases.trigger: coating damage missed because the check cadence was monthly, not per run
edge_cases.mitigation: per-run coating checks; a found breach is either repaired before use or quantified into the area facts; the stripped spine gold goes to reclaim

edge_cases.description: A piece drops off its hook into the tank mid-run
edge_cases.trigger: fatigued spring or undersized hook releasing under agitation
edge_cases.mitigation: shut down per the equipment's instructions before retrieval, recover with a non-conductive tool under the handling obligations, re-prep the piece fully, and log the fixture for maintenance

edge_cases.description: The rectifier faults with a nickel-plated load activated and waiting for gold
edge_cases.trigger: an unplanned delay stranding a perishable surface mid-line
edge_cases.mitigation: into the holding rinse immediately, reactivate per the upstream product's instructions once the line recovers, and log the delay and reactivation against the batch

edge_cases.description: Silicated cleaner carry-over gels in the acid dip and the batch later shows haze and peel
edge_cases.trigger: insufficient rinsing after a silicate-bearing cleaner
edge_cases.mitigation: encode the hot double rinse after silicated cleaners in the sequence diagram and gate the acid entry on rinse conductivity

edge_cases.description: An acid-line rinse bucket and a cyanide-line rinse bucket are found sharing a sink drain
edge_cases.trigger: convenience plumbing or a borrowed vessel crossing the segregation line
edge_cases.mitigation: hard stop of the line; physically separate the vessels, plumbing and travel paths before any work resumes; review against formal training and jurisdiction rules and log the near-miss

edge_cases.description: The dead rinse ahead of gold has concentrated until work passing through it carries contamination into the bath
edge_cases.trigger: recovery value hoarded past the rinse's functional limit
edge_cases.mitigation: put a conductivity reading and refresh threshold on the dead rinse like any gate; send the spent charge to reclaim on schedule

edge_cases.description: An under-filled barrel load loses part-to-part contact and a fraction of the parts come out patchily bare
edge_cases.trigger: load below the barrel's minimum working fraction
edge_cases.mitigation: respect the equipment's minimum load fraction, combine compatible lots to reach it, or route the small lot to rack; inspect barrel lots for pale parts before release

edge_cases.description: A mirror flash lot is fingerprinted during unracking by bare hands
edge_cases.trigger: glove discipline dropped at the last step of a finished run
edge_cases.mitigation: gloves or cots until pieces are boxed, soft trays at the unracking station, and the no-touch obligation posted where unracking happens

edge_cases.description: Stop-off lacquer lifts in the hot cleaner two tanks before gold and the two-tone boundary bleeds
edge_cases.trigger: mask compatibility assumed instead of tested against the full tank sequence
edge_cases.mitigation: coupon-test every mask product against the actual sequence before first production use and record the tested pairing in the plan

workflow.action: Translate the job sheet into a written run plan
workflow.description: Fix route candidate, tank order, fixture, contact zones, masking and carried compliance flags before any handling
workflow.gate: route, tank order, fixture, contact zones, masking and compliance flags all named; unfixturable pieces flagged for escalation

workflow.description: Group only jobs sharing chemistry sequence, deposit spec, geometry class and handling class
workflow.artifact: closed batch list with piece count and area classes
workflow.gate: one spec per run and the area list closed before amps are computed

workflow.description: Run the rack/barrel/brush fitness test and record the decision with its reason, testing boundary cases on sacrifice pieces
workflow.gate: geometry, batch size and finish class each pass the chosen route's fitness test or the job re-routes or escalates

workflow.description: Write the per-piece-class contact plan and the mask plan with tested compatibility
workflow.gate: every contact hidden or sanctioned and sized to its current; every mask product coupon-tested against the sequence

workflow.description: Check continuity to every tip, coating, tip condition and grip; report exposed metal to the area facts
workflow.gate: continuity to every tip, coating intact or quantified, tips clean and gripping

workflow.description: Hang pieces on planned contacts at plan spacing, faces to anodes, venting tilts applied
workflow.gate: count, positions, orientation and venting verified against the plan before the first tank

workflow.action: Stage the line and set agitation
workflow.description: Confirm each tank's agitation class running per equipment instructions and every receiving station ready
workflow.gate: agitation running as planned per tank; mist control confirmed on any air-agitated nickel-bearing tank
